text:
maria: quick note — on the 2pm canary I noticed sustained RSS growth tied to KV reuse across sessions when contexts exceed ~64k tokens. Not a single big leak, more like fragmentation + small alloc churn.
ajay: ugh. was that on the cpu-side pager or gpu pinned memory?
maria: seems to be GPU pinned. profiler shows cache pages being sliced and reallocated instead of reused when prefix lengths vary slightly.
liam: do you have a minimal repro? can we replicate with synthetic traffic?
maria: yes — sending a mix of prefixes: same conversation prefix but occasional one-off system prompts. When the cache key includes the full prompt text it prevents reuse.
olivia: so cache key granularity is the culprit. what key are we using now?
maria: current key = sha1(model + sequence_length + prefix_text) which is too strict.
ajay: we should move to semantically stable keys: model + prefix_id + normalized_prefix_len_bucket + kv_version. That lets small variations reuse the same backing pages.
liam: agree. also we should consider prefix canonicalization (strip ephemeral tokens, collapse whitespace) + a short hash so long prompts don't bloat key maps.
maria: patched a quick experiment: key = sha1(model + prefix_sig) where prefix_sig is first-N tokens normalized + token_count_bucket. Results: cache hit rate up from 54% -> 88% on our chat trace and peak GPU mem steady.
dev-bot: profile-run completed: 1766123468 — delta RSS +1.2% over 30m with new key heuristics.
olivia: nice. did you measure fragmentation? any change in number of free slices?
maria: yes — defrag events dropped ~3x. Allocation histogram shows fewer tiny (>512B) slices. My theory: strict keys caused many small KV allocations tied to unique prompt suffixes, and the allocator couldn't coalesce.
ajay: two follow-ups: (1) add deterministic prefix hashing function in runtime util, (2) add experimental session-stickiness toggle to route repeated user sessions to same worker (improves reuse for short- lived sessions).
liam: on (2) watch out for load skew. session-stickiness could overload single worker. We should combine with a sticky window TTL and global balancing.
maria: noted. also adding a soft-eviction policy: prefer evicting pages with low reuse_count and large fragmentation cost. That reduced paging churn in sim.
olivia: can you paste the canonicalization snippet?
maria: sure:
```
# prefix_sig: normalize -> take first 128 tokens -> hash -> bucket by len
def prefix_sig(prefix_tokens):
    norm = [t.strip().lower() for t in prefix_tokens if t not in EPHEMERAL_TOKENS]
    head = norm[:128]
    return sha1(" ".join(head).encode()) + ":" + str(len(head)//32)
```
ajay: looks good. also recommend including model_quant and kv_layout_version in the key so we don't mix incompatible pages.
liam: perf test plan: A/B traffic on canary for 24h, synthetic long-context spike for 1h, measure hit-rate, GPU RSS, defrag events, p99 latency.
maria: adding dashboards and alerts. I'll push the prefix_sig util + config flag under feature.kv_loose_keys.
olivia: create runbook entry if we flip stickiness on: how to drain overloaded workers, TTL defaults, metric thresholds.
maria: will do. I'll also add a small regression test that simulates token-level variations and verifies reuse > 80%.
ajay: awesome. if it holds, we can default to loose keys for chat workloads and keep strict keys for deterministic evals. :thumbsup:
maria: filing follow-ups: GH#3521 (prefix hash util), GH#3522 (stickiness toggle + balancing), GH#3523 (eviction heuristic).
liam: thanks — let's sync tomorrow after 24h canary.
maria: thanks everyone.
